bug_description.normalized: During subsetting of an attacker-supplied font, `_gsub_closure` reaches `OT::SingleSubstFormat1::closure` and constructs `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter> iter (this+coverage)`. The new one-argument `hb_auto_t` constructor copies the GSUB Coverage object by value into its local parameter `t1` and initializes `Coverage::Iter` from that temporary. `Coverage::Iter::init` then forwards the selected coverage arm into a nested iterator that stores a pointer to the constructor-local copy, so once the constructor returns `iter.get_glyph()` reads glyph data through out-of-scope stack state. The poisoned `glyph_id` is passed into `hb_set_t::has`, stored into `page_map_t key` in `hb_set_t::page_for`, and finally consumed by the `else if (c > 0)` branch in `hb_vector_t::bfind()`, where MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value.

source.description: The vulnerable path first consumes the attacker-controlled GSUB Coverage table by passing `this+coverage` into the one-argument `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter>` constructor that materializes the loop iterator.
source.value_from: The fuzzed font's GSUB `SingleSubstFormat1` subtable provides the `coverage` offset resolved by `this+coverage` during `hb_subset(..., drop_ot_layout=false)`.

sink.description: MSan crash site. The binary-search branch tests comparison result `c`, which was derived from a `page_map_t key` built from the poisoned glyph id.

root_cause.description: The one-argument `hb_auto_t` constructor takes the Coverage object by value, creating constructor-local copy `t1` and initializing `Coverage::Iter` from that temporary instead of from the original table view. That by-value materialization is the lifetime bug that leaves the iterator reading through out-of-scope stack state after the constructor returns.

parser_admitted.description: When `drop_ot_layout` is false, the subset planner calls `_gsub_closure(face, initial_gids_to_retain)` and enters GSUB closure on the attacker-controlled face.

tainted_value_origin.description: MemorySanitizer reports that the uninitialized value was created by the stack allocation of local `iter` in `SingleSubstFormat1::closure`; the bad lifetime is introduced while that stack object is initialized through `hb_auto_t`'s by-value constructor.

coarse_trace.summary: The subset planner enters GSUB closure on the attacker-controlled face and dispatches into `OT::SingleSubstFormat1::closure` with a populated retained-glyph set.

The closure constructs `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter>` from `this+coverage`; the new by-value constructor initializes the iterator from a temporary Coverage copy, so `iter.get_glyph()` later reads glyph data through dead stack-backed state.
The poisoned glyph id is converted into a `page_map_t key` for retained-glyph lookup, and `hb_vector_t::bfind()` branches on a comparison result derived from that poisoned key.

fine_trace.note: The closure resolves the attacker-controlled `coverage` offset from the fuzzed GSUB subtable and uses it to construct local iterator `iter`. This is the first project statement on the crashing path that materializes vulnerability-relevant state from the font data.

The one-argument `hb_auto_t` constructor receives `this+coverage` by value, creating ctor-local copy `t1`, then calls `Coverage::Iter::init(t1)`. This is the regression step: iterator initialization is now driven from a temporary stack copy instead of the original coverage object.

fine_trace.code: switch (format) { case 1: u.format1.init (c_.u.format1); return; case 2: u.format2.init (c_.u.format2); return; }
fine_trace.note: Iterator initialization selects the copied coverage format and forwards the chosen union arm from ctor-local `t1` into the nested iterator. Both nested iterator init routines store `c = &c_`, so `iter` retains a pointer into the constructor-local copy rather than into the original GSUB coverage table.

After the `hb_auto_t` constructor has finished, `iter.get_glyph()` dereferences the nested iterator state that points into the expired ctor-local copy and materializes a poisoned `glyph_id`. This is the first scalar value pulled from the stale iterator and forwarded toward the crash.

The poisoned glyph id is passed into the retained-glyph set membership test. `_populate_gids_to_retain` seeded the set with glyph 0 before GSUB closure, so `has()` performs a real `page_for(glyph_id)` lookup on a populated set.

The set lookup derives page-map search key `key.major` from poisoned glyph id `g`. MSan's secondary stack explicitly reports this line as the store where the uninitialized value is written into `key` before the final branch use.
The poisoned page-map key is forwarded unchanged into the binary search over the retained-glyph page map.
The binary search compares `x.major` from the poisoned key against `arrayZ[mid].major` and produces tainted comparison result `c`.
MSan sink. The binary-search branch consumes tainted comparison result `c` and reports use-of-uninitialized-value at this control-flow use.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` / `fixed_commit` only add subset headers to `src/Makefile.sources` for distcheck and do not modify `hb-dsalgs.hh`, `hb-ot-layout-gsub-table.hh`, `hb-ot-layout-common.hh`, `hb-set.hh`, or `hb-vector.hh`, so they do not demonstrate a fix for the witnessed MSan bug.

format.name: OpenType font
format.contract: A font blob that loads as an `hb_face_t` and, during `hb_subset(..., drop_ot_layout=false)`, reaches `OT::SingleSubstFormat1::closure` and executes `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter> iter (this+coverage)` so `iter.get_glyph()` reads a glyph id through the iterator state initialized from the constructor-local Coverage copy.
